chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Yasir the servant, who said: I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him):
'Will the month of Ramadan be twenty-nine days?' He replied: 'Indeed, the month of Ramadan will not be less than thirty days.'
ai.seo_question: Is the month of Ramadan always thirty days or can it be twenty-nine?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the lunar calendar by asserting that Ramadan is invariably thirty days, distinguishing it from the variable twenty-nine-day months. This statement serves as a key indicator of the Imam's divine knowledge (*'ilam*) and authority, reinforcing the precision of the Islamic lunar cycle as understood in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the reliability of the Ahl al-Bayt in preserving the exact timing of religious obligations.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 21-4 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Yasir - the servant (of Imam Al-Ridha (MGB)), “I asked Al-Ridha (MGB), ‘Would the month of Ramazan ever be twenty-nine days?’’
The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘No. The month of Ramazan will never be less than thirty days.’”
